guidance: Engraving estimate, not a finished layout. Even spacing and a fixed staff size are assumed, while titles, page numbers, ragged bottoms and actual system spacing all change what fits: enter the measurements of the real edition and check the proof before printing.
method: A system is one line of a score: every staff played together, joined by a bracket or brace. Casting off is the decision of how many systems go on a page, and vertically it is decided by the staves rather than by the notes. The staff is five lines with four spaces between them, so the staff height is four staff spaces, and the point used here is the printers' point of 2540/7227 mm, so a 20 pt staff is 7.03 mm high and one staff space is 1.7573 mm. The page's printable height is the paper height less the top and bottom margins, the margins being measured from the paper edge to the printable area. A system's block is staves x staff height plus the gap between staves counted in staff spaces, which repeats between every pair of adjacent staves; the vertical pitch of a system is that block plus the gap between systems, also in staff spaces. Systems per page is one plus the number of further pitches that fit in the printable height after the first block, which is the exact floor rather than an approximation, and the page count is the systems divided by that capacity rounded up, with the last page short by construction. The full-page figure reports how much of the printable height the systems use and how much is left below the last one. Paper sizes are the ISO 216 A4, A5 and B4 sheets and US Letter at 8.5 by 11 inches, all in millimetres; landscape swaps width and height. The model assumes equal spacing between systems and between staves, so it answers for a page of evenly set systems, and it counts no title block, instrument names or page number: LilyPond treats a title as a system, so its height belongs in the top margin or the systems count, and ragged-bottom settings leave the last page short by design. It says nothing about page turns, which depend on rests. Staff heights from 8 to 32 points, 1 to 24 staves, margins up to 100 mm, gaps up to 40 and 60 staff spaces and 1 to 999 systems are accepted, each with its own refusal; a single system taller than the printable page is refused with its measured height rather than printed as zero systems per page.
